## Principle PYTHIA is trying to solve the space structurally, not search it blindly. This is not “search first, optimize later.” It is: - Solve first — use structure, compression, and inference to collapse the search space - Search only as fallback — when the structure does not collapse cleanly, fall back to brute-force --- ## Runtime Hierarchy
Layer Role What Happens Here
1. PULVINI substrate Compress, fold, persist, restore Memory compression, reversible fold/unfold, checkpoint/state persistence, worker restart continuity, telemetry/state normalization
2. State / tensor / memory Retain useful structure Long-horizon state retention, multi-worker shared memory maps, persistent “best known” structures between runs
3. Chronos solver Infer, collapse, prioritize, solve Consume compressed/folded state, operate on structured manifolds, produce candidate collapse / prioritization signals
4. Mining execution Validate, submit, measure Stratum, share validation, block submission, hashrate measurement
--- ## Hot-Path Rule - Validity stays exact — share validation, difficulty check, and submission are never touched by experimental math - Solving intelligence sits before brute-force effort — the solve path runs first, the fallback search path runs only if the solve path doesn’t collapse cleanly - Search is fallback, not identity — PYTHIA is a solver that searches when needed, not a searcher that happens to solve --- ## Solve Path vs Fallback Search Path ### Solve Path (runs first)
Step Module Function Output
S1 DataFoldingEngine / GoldenTransform Precondition inputs and state — fold worker state, reduce active memory footprint, preserve recoverability Compressed state vector
S2 TransfiniteMemoryMapper Load persisted checkpoint — restore best-known search position from prime-gap-indexed store Restored nonce region + resonance history
S3 QuantumCoherenceAnalyzer Assess solve regime quality — is the current state in a high-quality solve regime? Coherence gate: trust structured inference or fall back
S4 MandelbrotResonanceEngine Identify phase-stable nonce regions — manifold guidance for candidate collapse Stable nonce region candidates
S5 GoldenQuantumInfinityFold Multi-level candidate collapse — search across fold levels for structured nonce candidates Prioritized candidate list
S6 Chronos solver Collapse and prioritize — consume folded state, produce final candidate list Ranked nonce candidates
### Fallback Search Path (runs only if solve path doesn’t collapse cleanly)
Step Module Function Trigger
F1 GoldenQuantumComputer Golden-ratio enhanced Grover search Coherence gate says “low-quality solve regime” or candidate list empty
F2 GoldenRatioMining Direct golden nonce selection Solve path + F1 both fail to produce candidates
F3 Brute-force increment Classical nonce increment All structured paths exhausted — never removed, always available
--- ## Module → Runtime Position Map
Module Runtime Layer Path What It Does in PYTHIA
TransfiniteMemoryMapper 1. PULVINI Solve (S2) Checkpoint store, session persistence, prime-gap-indexed memory
DataFoldingEngine 1. PULVINI Solve (S1) Reversible fold/unfold of worker state, telemetry compression
GoldenTransform 1. PULVINI Solve (S1) Lossless compression, preconditioning, transport/storage cost reduction
GoldenConstants / UCI 0. Config All Single source of mathematical configuration, consistent runtime semantics, avoid drift in scaling assumptions
MandelbrotResonanceEngine 3. Chronos Solve (S4) Phase-stable nonce region identification, manifold guidance
QuantumCoherenceAnalyzer 3. Chronos Solve (S3) Solve regime quality assessment, coherence gate
GoldenQuantumInfinityFold 3. Chronos Solve (S5) Multi-level nonce region search, candidate collapse
GoldenQuantumComputer 4. Mining Fallback (F1) Golden-ratio enhanced search when solve path doesn’t collapse
GoldenRatioMining 4. Mining Fallback (F2) Direct golden nonce selection, last structured resort
InfinityGPU Future — Mathematical processing abstraction, not wired yet
--- ## What to Measure
Metric What It Measures Target
Memory reduction RAM saved by folding/compression vs raw state > 50% reduction per worker
Recovery quality after restart Time to 90% of pre-restart hashrate Faster than cold start
Time to productive state Seconds from worker start to first share-worthy candidate Decreasing over time as checkpoints accumulate
Candidate quality improvement % of candidates from solve path vs fallback Solve path % increasing over time
Effective throughput per worker Shares/min per worker ≥ baseline (no regression)
Fewer wasted cycles Hashes before share-worthy candidate Decreasing as solve path matures
--- ## Wiring Priority (Solve-First Order) 1. PULVINI substrate — wire DataFoldingEngine + TransfiniteMemoryMapper for checkpoint persistence and state folding 2. Golden transform / lifting — wire GoldenTransform for preconditioning and compression 3. Infinity fold / transfinite memory — wire GoldenQuantumInfinityFold for long-horizon state retention and multi-worker shared maps 4. Coherence / validation — wire QuantumCoherenceAnalyzer as the coherence gate (trust structured inference vs brute-force fallback) 5. Constants / UCI — wire GoldenConstants as single source of mathematical configuration 6. Chronos solver — wire MandelbrotResonanceEngine + Chronos as the solver engine (not a search ornament) 7. Mining execution — validate, submit, measure (unchanged hot path) 8. Fallback search — wire GoldenQuantumComputer + GoldenRatioMining as fallback only --- ## Summary PYTHIA is trying to solve the space structurally, not search it blindly. The solve path runs first. Search is fallback, not identity. Validity stays exact.
